constant_fields_refused: resentment_score: degenerate fit: every household in one cell

company_churn_estimate.why: `estimate_renewal_churn` takes an old rate AND a new one, so it exists at a renewal and nowhere else

company_eac_kwh.why: the company's own estimate of annual consumption, from twelve months of its own billing -- held continuously, previously written only at renewal

discount_pct.why: an offer artefact -- there is no discount without an offer

expected_term_margin_gbp.why: priced at the offer, against the offer's own term

mean_recent_margin_rate.why: the portfolio position the pricing chain reads at every priced term, carried by `account_state_log` since 2026-09-06

perceived_bill_saving_gbp.why: a renewal-window quantity: what THIS renewal appears to save against the rate it replaced

rate_vs_svt_pct.why: the spread between the two above

resentment_score.why: the journey register advances in a renewal window; an account with no renewal has no journey to read

svt_rate_gbp_per_mwh.why: the published default-tariff cap on the day, PER FUEL. Read this field's coverage against the run that produced it: until 2026-09-06 the world wrote it for electricity legs only, so 146-of-164 was a missing READ and not the field's own scope

unit_rate_gbp_per_mwh.why: what the company charges this account now

magnitude_shrunk_toward_the_null.what_it_assumes: that a best-of-N selection inflates a real effect by as much as it inflates pure noise. Under a real effect the winner is chosen on signal more often, so the true inflation is smaller and this figure over-corrects. Reported as a floor on the magnitude, never as the magnitude.

magnitude_three_way_split.refused: three-way split needs 8 households per cell on the fit fold and 20 on the estimate fold; this rung gives 5.00 per cell from a fit fold of 20 and an estimate fold of 19. The reading beside this refusal is reported because the direction of travel is evidence; it is not an estimate and must not be gated on.

single_feature_ceilings.refused: degenerate fit: every household in one cell

we_cannot_tell.on_the_magnitude: AND THE SIZE OF IT IS NOT ESTABLISHED, which is a separate claim from whether it is real. +0.5760 is the largest of a search ranked on the very fold it is then reported from, so it is biased up as an estimate however cleanly it clears a null. De-biasing it needs a third fold — fit on one, choose on a second, score on a third — and this rung cannot carry one: 5.0 households per cell on the fit fold against the 8 this instrument requires. Forced through anyway it reads -0.0452, inside a noise floor of +0.2701 (p=0.7761) — the direction of travel, and not an estimate. The full-coverage rung CAN carry the split, and there the estimate is +0.2992, inside its own noise floor of +0.1557 (p=0.005) — indistinguishable from nothing. Holding the fit fold at the same size and separating ONLY the choosing from the reporting moves the figure from +0.3362 to -0.0452, so +0.3814 of it is the search and nothing else — one variable, measured, not inferred. The rotations do not even agree on which candidate wins, and their estimates run from -0.3686 to +0.1446: which pair is 'best' is a fact about who landed on the ranking side of the split. So R1's ceiling clears its null on this book and its MAGNITUDE has no unbiased estimate here. A49 gates R3 and R4 on this instrument and must read the magnitude field, which is null — not +0.5760. What closes it is COVERAGE, not a re-run.
we_cannot_tell.statement: WE CANNOT TELL. The headline figure of +0.5760 is the winner of a 45-way search, and when the SAME search is re-run against 200 shuffled worlds -- households' true sensitivities dealt out at random -- the winner reaches +0.5806 at the 95th percentile and matched or beat the real figure in 12 of them (p=0.0647). The measurement cannot separate this ceiling from chance, so we report no ceiling.
we_cannot_tell.what_it_does_not_say: This is not a finding that price sensitivity is unlearnable. It is a refusal to distinguish, which is a different claim. The pair rung carries 69 households, and at that size only a ceiling above +0.5806 can be told from chance at all -- so a real effect of moderate size is invisible to this instrument either way. The separate full-coverage rung (n=164) reads cannot tell on the same correction, and the two rungs disagreeing is itself a reason to hold the number loosely. And the winning fit scores 0.5760 on households it never saw against 0.1977 on the ones it was built from -- 2.9 times better out of sample than in it. A fit does not do that; a search over 45 candidates ranked by the out-of-sample score finds one that does. This is not evidence the ceiling is chance -- the winner of a shuffled world overshoots its own fit for the same reason -- so the p-value above stands. It is the one thing that p-value cannot see, and it is why this figure is reported as the best of a search rather than as a bound.
